rows.locus: cement handle op --input {} exits 2 through the _UsageError channel, not through a dispatch branch
rows.probe: tmp=$(mktemp -d); uv run cement --db "$tmp/db" --partition p handle op --input '{}' 2>"$tmp/err"; rc=$?; jq -r '[input_filename, .error, .message] | @tsv' "$tmp/err"; printf 'rc=%s\n' "$rc"; rm -rf "$tmp"
rows.reading: Removal must reject the exact handle leaf during root parsing, before any System dispatch can run.
rows.baseline: At 4e33cc6 the parser accepts handle; an unregistered operation reaches dispatch and exits 3 with error=not_found and message='operation is not registered in this partition'.
rows.expected: Exit 2; stderr JSON has error='invalid' and message beginning "argument command: invalid choice: 'handle'"; no System.handle call occurs.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. `handle` is no longer a choice of the `command` subparser, so argparse refuses it before any dispatch code runs. Routing through `_UsageError` rather than a dispatch branch is the whole point: a dispatch-branch refusal would mean the leaf still exists and merely declines.
